title: Route-level A/B testing — weekly notes (2026 W06)
content:
Week: 2026 W06 (Feb 2–Feb 8)

TL;DR
- Dogfood is generating useful feedback but also highlighting copy/UX gaps around start/stop, “control” semantics, and what gets logged.
- Biggest beta risks are instrumentation completeness + metric mismatch (cardinality + sampling + missing dimensions) and guardrail automation + runbook readiness.
- We should treat “results UI” as read-only + clearly labeled beta until we have end-to-end validation across gateway → ingestion → aggregation → UI.

What we were trying to accomplish this week
1) Close the instrumentation gaps blocking trustworthy experiment results.
2) Align guardrail thresholds + alert routing with SRE so beta doesn’t create an on-call surprise.
3) Incorporate dogfood feedback into the create/start/stop flow and terminology.

Progress / status

1) Beta readiness checklist (current view)
- Deterministic assignment stability (retries + stream reconnect): PARTIAL
  - We still see occasional variant flips on stream reconnect in staging when client does not send stable identity header.
  - Action: doc + UI warning + maybe add server-side fallback key (see “Instrumentation gaps”).
- Exposure logging emitted from gateway: IN PROGRESS
  - Emission in PR, but schema validation + sampling strategy needs final alignment.
- Latency + TTFT breakdown by experiment_id/variant: IN PROGRESS
  - Latency tagging landed but we need to confirm: TTFT present for streaming only? also end-to-end vs model latency.
- Cost attribution by experiment_id/variant: IN PROGRESS
  - Cost tagging exists; need to verify aggregation matches billing/metering semantics.
- Aggregation jobs/materialized views: NOT READY
  - UI will be blocked without stable query endpoints + performant rollups.
- Guardrails + auto-rollback hook: IN PROGRESS
  - Hook exists; needs integration with “disable experiment quickly” path + alerts.
- Audit events for lifecycle actions: IN PROGRESS
  - Basic create/update/start/stop/rollback coverage is close; still validating required fields with Security.
- Docs for beta partners + Support troubleshooting: NEEDS UPDATE
  - Dogfood showed multiple misconfigurations we should preempt.

2) Design feedback from internal dogfood (top items)
Sources: #eng thread (1707165520), ad-hoc sessions w/ DevEx + internal users

A. Create experiment flow is “too easy to do something scary”
- People expect a stronger “Validate” step before Start.
- Ask: add explicit preflight checks (route exists, model variants resolvable, capacity tier compatible, and “overlapping rollout” warnings).
- Proposed UX change (Kenji/Tessa):
  - Step 1: Define (route + eligibility + variants + split)
  - Step 2: Validate (shows computed assignment key, shows what will be logged, shows estimated exposure rate)
  - Step 3: Start (requires typing experiment name / confirms guardrails enabled)

B. Terminology: “Control / Variant” is confusing
- Feedback: Some teams want “A / B” only; others want to label “baseline / candidate”.
- Support escalated: user thought “control” meant “no experiment” or “safe path”.
- Proposal:
  - UI: label as “Variant A (baseline)” and “Variant B (candidate)” by default.
  - Advanced: allow custom labels, but enforce uniqueness + character limits.

C. Overlapping rollouts / precedence confusion
- Dogfood testers didn’t understand interaction with canaries/fallbacks.
- Need UI to warn:
  - “This route already has an active canary rollout.”
  - “Fallback policy may override experiment assignment on errors/overload.”
- We should add a small “Routing precedence” help link and show a simplified decision order.

D. Results dashboard: confidence indicators and sample size
- Users asked “is 2% faster meaningful?”
- Need to add more explicit copy:
  - “Beta: results are directional; check exposure volume + time window.”
  - Show minimum sample warnings (esp for p99 and error rate deltas).
- Sana/Jonas asked that we avoid implying statistical significance until we ship the stats plan + multiple comparisons guardrails.

3) Instrumentation gaps / data quality issues (beta blockers)

A. Exposure event schema fields (missing/unclear)
- We need a consistent set of dims across exposure, latency, and cost so joins work.
- Gaps observed:
  - experiment_id + variant_id present, but route_id vs raw path inconsistent between gateway and console.
  - region present but not normalized (eu-west-1 vs EUW1 in some internal dashboards).
  - streaming flag sometimes missing, causing mixing TTFT vs non-stream metrics.
  - retry_count / reconnect indicator not available; makes variant flip debugging hard.

B. Assignment key stability vs privacy
- Current dogfood clients don’t always send a stable user key.
- If we hash on api_key_id only, some customers will not get “user-level” stickiness (fine), but retries should still stick.
- Ask from platform/routing: define exact precedence for assignment key components.
- Open question: should Console show “what key is used” (e.g., api_key_id only) so customers understand what they’re measuring?

C. Sampling + cardinality guardrails
- Logan/Allison flagged risk that adding experiment tags everywhere blows up metrics.
- Need final allowlist:
  - allowed tags: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, project_id (maybe), region, deployment_mode
  - explicitly NOT allowed: raw customer headers, raw path, prompt hash
- We still need to decide sampling policy for exposure events (100% vs sampled).
  - If exposure is sampled but latency/cost are not, results UI will be confusing.
  - If we sample everything, p99 + error rates get noisy.
  - Current leaning: exposure = 100% (cheap log event), metrics = aggregated counters/histograms only (no per-request log), with strict dims.

D. Metric mismatch report (internal)
- Not a customer ticket yet, but we reproduced “Console p95 differs from Grafana by ~10–15%” on the same time window.
- Possible causes:
  - different definitions (gateway e2e vs model time)
  - window alignment + ingestion delay
  - mixing streaming/non-stream requests
- Action: write down canonical definitions in the “Validate” step and in docs.

4) SRE / guardrails readiness
- SRE wants minimum guardrails + an owner/plan for rollback automation.
- Proposed default guardrails for beta (subject to SRE signoff):
  - error rate: +0.5% absolute increase vs baseline for 10 min window
  - 429s: +0.2% absolute increase vs baseline OR absolute threshold > 0.5%
  - p95 e2e latency: +10% relative increase vs baseline for 15 min window
  - capacity saturation signals: if variant B hits capacity policy warnings, auto-shift to baseline
- Alert routing:
  - Guardrail violation alerts → #eng-sre + paging only if customer-impacting thresholds exceeded.
  - Non-paging warnings for early beta: #eng-platform + #console-rollouts.
- Still missing:
  - end-to-end runbook validation in staging (disable experiment + confirm metrics recovery).
  - “who approves enabling beta flag per account/region”.

Decisions made this week
- UI will include an explicit Validate step; Start will be blocked if Validate fails.
- We will show a “Beta / directional” label on results until aggregation definitions are stable and validated.
- Variant labels default to “baseline / candidate” language, with optional custom labels.

Open questions
1) What’s the definitive routing precedence order between (a) canary rollouts, (b) route-level experiment, (c) fallback policies? We need to show it in UI and enforce it in policy engine.
2) What is the minimum required assignment key to guarantee stickiness across retry/stream reconnect without PII?
3) Are we comfortable with 100% exposure logging for beta (retention + access controls)? If not, what do we sample and how do we explain results?
4) Do we gate beta to Hosted + Dedicated only, or allow Private behind a separate flag? (Marissa leaning to gate Private.)

Action items (next week)
- Chloe: Add server-side validation checks for route + variant config; return actionable errors for UI (target: Wed).
- Jada/Jordan: Finalize assignment key precedence + write short spec snippet for Console “what key is used” display (target: Thu).
- Logan/Allison: Publish final tag allowlist + sampling recommendation + definitions for e2e latency/TTFT (target: Thu).
- Nadia: Confirm cost attribution semantics for experiments match metering (target: Fri).
- Kenji/Tessa: Update create flow prototype with Validate step + overlap warnings + improved copy for control/baseline (target: Wed for review).
- Sean: Review proposed guardrail thresholds + confirm alert routing + sign off on minimum runbook requirements (target: Fri).
- Dylan: Draft beta readiness checklist (GA-style) and share with Marissa + Priya for gating decision (target: Fri).

Notes / randoms
- Dogfood request: “Pause experiment” vs Stop. Current thinking: Stop ends exposure; Pause keeps config but stops routing. Might be out of scope for beta, but we should clarify semantics now so we don’t paint ourselves into a corner.
- We need a “copy/paste config” view for debugging (masked). People keep asking “what exactly is active right now?”

References
- Linear: ENG-2842 (exposure schema + ingestion), ENG-2844 (aggregation jobs), ENG-2845 (dashboards + alerts), ENG-2848 (beta rollout plan)
- PRs: pr_18415 (latency by experiment), pr_18403 (cost attribution), pr_18459 (guardrail evaluator), pr_18519 (reduce metric cardinality)
- Slack threads: eng/1707165520 (dogfood feedback), eng-sre/1707334988 (guardrails), support/1707779901 (control semantics confusion)
